_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.

candidates.why: NEW THIS WEEK, AND THE FIRST TTS CANDIDATE THIS FILE HAS EVER CARRIED THAT RUNS ON BOTH MACHINES. WHAT IT REPLACES AND BY HOW MUCH, against the two TTS services actually running on BeTenshi. Against ChatterboxMultilingual on :8004 (the cloning service, 3.0 GB measured resident): CV3 English cloning 2.02 WER against 3.42 (41% lower), SIM 63.23 against 53.13 (+10.10), RTFx 65.96 against 0.99 — SIXTY-SEVEN TIMES the throughput — and 43 declared languages against 23. Install Audio8 first if intelligibility is what :8004 is for; install this one if a cloned voice has to sound like the speaker, answer in near-real time, or speak one of the twenty languages Audio8 does not. WHICH MACHINE — AND THIS IS THE REASON IT EARNS A SLOT THAT NO LEADERBOARD ROW COULD GIVE IT: the authors ship FOUR runtimes for one set of weights, named on the card — a CUDA server for NVIDIA, AN MLX SERVER FOR APPLE SILICON, a C++/ggml server and CLI (CPU, CUDA, Metal or Vulkan), and a WebGPU browser build. So it runs on BETENSHI (cuda, sm_120) AND ON B5 (metal, 128 GB unified) from the same repo, with no `runtimes` pin, which is why none is set. B5's tts today is the MLX Qwen3-TTS-CustomVoice build the 09-11 report dropped as a candidate, and it does NOT clone — so on B5 this is a new capability, not a swap. SGLang-Omni serves it behind the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint with streaming and reference-clip cloning (`sgl-omni serve --model-path Zyphra/ZONOS3-Mini`), which is the exact interface config/ai-router.yaml already fronts for local-kokoro and local-chatterbox — so wiring is an alias and a port, not an adapter. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: nobody has run it here, no Arabic figure exists on any board (CV3-Eval does not test Arabic, and 43 declared languages is a claim by the authors, not a measurement), and the repo is seven days old. ADOPTION, 30-DAY METRIC: 39,862 downloads and 408 likes, which is also its all-time total since the repo was created 09-11, and the top trending text-to-speech repo on the hub today. Again: that is attention, and the board is the evidence.

candidates.why: THE FIRST ENTRY THE `world` LANE HAS EVER HAD, AND THE FIRST THING TO SAY IS WHAT IT IS NOT. docs/models.md defines this lane as 'interactive, playable video' and says to rank it on 'the authors' fps and latency on a named GPU'. PAN 2 IS NOT PLAYABLE AND PUBLISHES NEITHER NUMBER: it is a 50-step diffusion sampler at 704x1248 and 24 fps producing up to 20 s a run, with CFG 2.5 on every step and one worker holding the full 29B model. So the lane's ranking basis cannot be applied, and if 'world' here means a model you can play, this lane is still empty. WHAT IT IS INSTEAD, AND WHY IT IS WORTH A SLOT: an ACTION-CONDITIONED world model. It takes a current observation (an optional image plus text) and actions described in text, and simulates the outcome as video — the Generative Latent Prediction architecture from 'Critique of World Models', where a language model writes the next world state as a structured, time-grounded description of events, timed actions bound to actors and camera motion, and a 29B MMDiT trained from scratch on hundreds of millions of videos annotated in that format renders what the description leaves open. WHAT IT WOULD LET THE OWNER MAKE THAT NEITHER BOX CAN MAKE TODAY, which is the bar for an empty lane: A SHOT THAT ANSWERS 'WHAT HAPPENS IF'. The five video models in ComfyUI (Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B, Wan 2.2 14B, LTX-2.5, HunyuanVideo 1.5, MiniMax H3) all take a prompt or a frame and hallucinate forward; none of them takes a world state and an action and predicts the consequence, and none of them can be asked the same question twice with different actions and give comparably different answers. For the Video Forge and Montage that is the difference between generating a shot and simulating a scene. WHY IT IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT A NOTE, WHICH IS ENTIRELY ABOUT LICENCE AND PACKAGING: apache-2.0 and ungated on BOTH repos, which is what has kept this lane's neighbours out all autumn — every alternative on the hub's video trending list today is a MiniMax-H3 derivative (hyperflow-h3-flash, Pika-H3-Flex, Open-H3-Regenerate-2K, the H3 LoRAs and GGUF repacks), and docs/models.md rules that family out because MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 is `license: other` and grants no rights in the USA, EU, UK or South Korea, which every derivative inherits. And Comfy-Org repacked it YESTERDAY into diffusion-single-file form with a folder layout in its README, which is the same pattern that turned speridlabs/idol into a real option (note 14): BeTenshi runs ComfyUI on :8188. WHICH MACHINE, AND THE TWO ANSWERS ARE OPPOSITE FOR OPPOSITE REASONS. BETENSHI (31.8 GB VRAM beside 63.3 GB host RAM): the stack is here and the memory is marginal — 30.7 GB of a 31.8 GB card on an assumption about when ComfyUI frees the text encoder, so `fits alone` at best and `won't fit` if that assumption is wrong. B5 (one 128 GB unified pool): 37.84 GB would vanish into the pool, and it CANNOT RUN AT ALL — there is no ComfyUI on B5, its only image/video path is the Draw Things CLI that config/hosts/b5.json records as unverified and expected to fail, and the authors' reference environment is CUDA-13-only (torch cu132, flash-attn-4, quack-kernels). `runtimes: ["cuda"]` is set for that reason and is the honest pin: this is the one candidate where the machine with the memory is the machine that cannot execute it. ADOPTION, SAID HONESTLY BECAUSE IT IS ALMOST NOTHING: IFM/PAN2 has 335 downloads in the last 30 days and 342 all-time with 161 likes; the Comfy-Org repack has ZERO downloads on both metrics and 17 likes, because it is one day old. Per docs/models.md 5b that is not evidence either way, and here there is no board to fall back on — so this entry rests on the licence, the capability and the packaging, and says so.
